findings.summary: Canonical READY remained caller/config dependent: GIT_WORK_TREE redirection, weakened stat-cache settings, and core.fileMode=false could conceal modified governance/control bytes or modes while --require-ready returned READY.
Assume-unchanged and skip-worktree markers now fail before refresh on governance and control files; the NUL-safe parser also rejects related nonstandard index markers.
Staged, unstaged, untracked, ignored, newline-filename and staged index-vs-HEAD drift probes fail closed.
Committed allowlists, frozen request/schema/history and ancestry bindings, lifecycle/ACCEPT binding, duplicate identifiers and capability prohibitions remain intact.

commands: verify remote PR head, commit, tree and reviewed-content digest
construct legitimate synthetic READY/ACCEPT descendant and run canonical --require-ready
assume-unchanged, skip-worktree, staged, unstaged, untracked, ignored and newline-path probes
core.checkStat minimal and core.trustctime false same-size/same-mtime probe
retest ancestry, frozen controls, lifecycle, identifiers, acceptance and capability boundaries
conclusion: Round 9 resolves the index-visibility defect, but caller-controlled Git context and stat cache can still hide unreviewed tracked bytes. Validator-integrity remains CHANGES_REQUIRED.
